cases.reason: Concrete paid apprenticeship with contractor assignment and a currently open application window. Useful for sustained career advancement, subject to selection, documentation and travel requirements.
criticalDetails: Applications and all documents must be completed by September 30, 2026; applications reopen February 1, 2027. Submit documents to djeatcapplications@outlook.com before receiving online application instructions; document review may take a week. [Application instructions](https://djeatc68.com/apply/)

Required documents include a valid driver's license, second identification document, graduation evidence and DD-214 if applicable. The application costs $35, nonrefundable. The subsequent Personal Experience Form has a two-week completion deadline. [Application instructions](https://djeatc68.com/apply/)

Inside Wireman is a four-year apprenticeship, generally combining 40 hours of assigned contractor work with evening classes twice weekly and occasional Saturdays. The page lists starting pay of $22.70/hour, but gives inconsistent completion and journeyman figures of $37.01 and $49.35/hour. Confirm the applicable wage schedule. [Program details](https://djeatc68.com/inside-wireman-apprenticeship/)

Application payment requires a credit card; foreign transcripts require official translation. Applicants must travel within the jurisdiction. Marijuana-positive testing disqualifies applicants; a felony does not automatically exclude an Inside Wireman applicant. Contact: 303-295-1903, 5610 Logan Street, Denver. [Applicant FAQ](https://djeatc68.com/apply/applicant-faq/)
openQuestions: What are the current tuition, books, tools, dues and other participant costs, and what assistance is available?
What minimum age and additional academic requirements apply?
What are the current selection timeline, available placements and wage rates?

cases.reason: Substantial employment support embedded in residential addiction recovery. Appropriate for men seeking that combined program who can meet its work and residential requirements.
criticalDetails: Residents receive career counseling from entry, help securing permanent employment, advancement guidance and training referrals. Employment must be full-time, payroll-based and compatible with the program schedule; temporary, part-time and cash jobs are prohibited. [Work program](https://stepdenver.org/our-4-pillars/work/)

Eligibility includes men aged 18 or older with addiction who can work full-time, are sober at intake and accept screening and testing. The application page excludes specified severely violent or sexual offenses and recent suicide attempts. It also requires agreement not to receive outside financial support or listed government benefits. This is the provider's admission rule. [Admission requirements](https://stepdenver.org/apply/)

Apply by phone at 303-295-7837 or at 2029 Larimer Street, Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–noon. Accepted applicants enter at 2:30 p.m. There is no entry fee; after employment, published fees are $15/day, $75/week or $200/month, plus responsibility for food. [Application and costs](https://stepdenver.org/apply/)

There is no waiting list; beds vary daily and admission is first-come, first-served. The FAQ recommends five orientation days. Provider employment claims conflict: the FAQ reports 79% employed within 45 days, while the application page reports 74%; neither guarantees placement. [FAQ](https://stepdenver.org/program-faqs/), [Application](https://stepdenver.org/apply/)
openQuestions: Is a bed available, and how do the residential schedule and admission rules fit the individual's circumstances?
How are the daily, weekly and monthly fee options applied?
Which employment outcome figure is current, and what reporting period does it cover?

cases.reason: Useful individualized coaching for Emily Griffith students and alumni, but the supplied title could misleadingly suggest unrestricted community access.
criticalDetails: The college identifies students and alumni as its coaching audience. Services include resumes, interviews, job searches and applications, with online or in-person meetings by appointment only. [Career services](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)

Current students and graduates can use the scheduling link or email careerservices@emilygriffith.edu. Apprenticeship job seekers are directed to apprenticeship@emilygriffith.edu; prospective students to admissions@emilygriffith.edu. [Referral paths](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)

The page offers approved-employer postings and assistance with employer connections, so this is more than a generic job board. It lists 1860 Lincoln Street, Denver, and 720-423-4700. Coaching fees, available appointment dates and placement rates are not stated. [Service details](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/career-services-for-job-seekers/)
openQuestions: Can community members who are neither students nor alumni receive coaching, including through the apprenticeship contact?
Is coaching free for each eligible group, and how soon are appointments available?

cases.reason: Denver Day Works has verified 2026 funding, but the Bayaud listing is outdated and a current program-specific intake route was not established.
criticalDetails: ServiceSource confirms it incorporated programs and staff formerly operated by Bayaud Enterprises. Update the provider identity rather than treating the inaccessible Bayaud website as evidence that all services ended. [Provider announcement](https://servicesource.org/servicesource-launches-new-programs-in-colorado/)

Denver adopted resolution 26-0503 on May 18, 2026, adding $413,000 and extending ServiceSource's Denver Day Works contract through December 31, 2026. Funding covers participant wages and support, staffing and operations citywide. [Adopted contract amendment](https://denver.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?G=928A1C29-26D7-4A5D-8DD4-947A533B1CC6&GUID=C2549384-7B0D-4074-8F30-B120C114EBEE&ID=7974114&Options=&Search=)

Earlier city documentation describes supported work for people experiencing homelessness, linked with food, shelter and other services. This establishes the historical program model; it does not establish current eligibility or pay. [Earlier city program description](https://denver.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=D9F474CD-4A84-4F32-8E27-832BE4A9F6D1&ID=5957933&Options=&Search=)

ServiceSource's current Colorado office is 1550 Dover Street, Lakewood, 303-830-6885. This is a general inquiry route, not a verified Day Works intake site. [Current contact](https://servicesource.org/contact-us/)

The linked April 2026 program presentation returned an unavailable-page error. The source-page ceiling was reached before current enrollment instructions, costs, shift schedules and participant wages could be established.
openQuestions: Who handles Denver Day Works referrals, and where and when does intake occur?
Are participants currently being accepted, and what homelessness, residency, disability or documentation requirements apply?
What are the current wages, payment timing, available work hours, participant costs and transportation supports?

cases.reason: Strong local reentry employment pathway with a named Denver office, participant contact and published referral process.
criticalDetails: CEO Denver serves people recently released from incarceration. Contact CEODenver@ceoworks.org or 720-279-8489; office: 3532 Franklin Street, Suite S, Denver. Published hours are Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. [Denver office](https://www.ceoworks.org/locations/denver)

CEO's service model includes job-readiness training, paid transitional work, coaching and placement, advanced training and retention support. These describe the national model; specific Denver assignments and training availability need confirmation. [CEO service model](https://www.ceoworks.org/)

People on community supervision can obtain a parole/probation referral; CEO then invites them to scheduled orientation. Outside California, the published orientation checklist includes a completed referral form, release form, government photo ID, and Social Security card or birth certificate. [Participant enrollment](https://ceoworks.org/participants)

CEO conducts employer outreach and publishes one year of retention support after full-time employment. The reviewed intake pages do not specify Denver fees, starting wages, the next orientation or an available work slot. [Participant services](https://ceoworks.org/participants)
openQuestions: How recent must release be, and can someone without active parole or probation enroll?
What assistance is available when required identification is missing?
What are the next orientation, participant costs, current wages, payment schedule and expected time to paid work?

cases.reason: Useful paid transitional employment with substantial practical supports, but entry is mediated through corrections programming and several published operating details require confirmation.
criticalDetails: DEN describes eligibility for people preparing to leave the justice system or in transitional halfway programming who are already engaged in CDOC employment-readiness programs. CDOC and the operator identify and select participants. [Program eligibility](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)

The airport describes approximately 12 weeks of landside maintenance work outside secure areas, employment support, equipment, meals, clothing, hygiene supplies, van transportation and an RTD EcoPass where needed. [Program supports](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)

The airport page lists $23.75/hour but describes payment as both weekly and daily. It mentions a waitlist above 10 interested people while also describing capacity for 20 participants. These figures should not be promised as current terms. [Published operating details](https://www.flydenver.com/business-and-community/ceea/career-pathways/new-heights-pilot-program/)

The airport still names Bayaud, while a public ServiceSource post identifies a graduate of its DEN New Heights program, supporting continued operation under ServiceSource. [ServiceSource program post](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/servicesourceinc_meet-arthur-griggs-a-recent-graduate-of-activity-7457863072796323840-2Yw5)

A practical inquiry path is the person's CDOC transition contact and ServiceSource's Colorado office at 303-830-6885. The latter is a general office contact, not a verified direct enrollment line. [ServiceSource contact](https://servicesource.org/contact-us/)
openQuestions: Which CDOC or ServiceSource staff member currently accepts referrals, and are places available?
What are the current wages, payment frequency, work schedule, capacity and any participant costs?
Can previously released people outside CDOC transitional programming qualify?

cases.reason: A free, specialized career-advancement pathway for eligible refugees and immigrants with sufficient English and financial stability for sustained participation.
criticalDetails: CAREERS requires approximately one to two years and does not target immediate employment. Support includes career planning, credential/licensure navigation, coaching, tutoring, foreign-transcript evaluation guidance and funding applications. [Program details](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)

Published entry categories include current Emily Griffith English students at levels 4/5, interest in its CTE programs, or foreign experience in engineering, barbering or cosmetology. Participants also need intermediate English or higher, work authorization or a pathway to employment, and a job or other financial stability. [Eligibility](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)

Email immigrant.services@emilygriffith.edu with name, phone number and career background or goal for eligibility screening and orientation. Meetings are weekly or biweekly, online or in person, during business hours. The program is free for eligible students and offers scholarships; full training-cost coverage is not promised. [Enrollment, schedule and costs](https://www.emilygriffith.edu/careers-for-refugees-and-immigrants/)
openQuestions: How are the listed eligibility alternatives applied, particularly for people pursuing training outside Emily Griffith?
Are orientations and navigator places available, and what scholarship amounts or uncovered credential costs apply?

cases.reason: Important public disability-employment infrastructure worth referring to for assessment and longer-term support, with a prominent waitlist limitation.
criticalDetails: DVR supports Coloradans with disabilities seeking, keeping or advancing in employment. Listed services include vocational counseling, training, job development/coaching, benefits planning, assistive technology and accommodations. Begin with the homepage's Online Request for Services to connect with a local office, or CDLE_voc.rehab@state.co.us. [DVR services and intake](https://dvr.colorado.gov/)

A January 28, 2026 state notice places newly eligible applicants and eligible people without an employment plan on a waitlist. Existing employment plans and student pre-employment transition services continue; applications and eligibility assessments remain available. Release follows disability priority and application order. [State waitlist notice](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/CODLE/bulletins/4065f78)

The April 8, 2026 state newsletter confirms an active waitlist exceeding 2,100 eligible people at that time. No later verified status change was found; this count is not a September estimate. [April update](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/CODLE/bulletins/40dedf6)

DVR's published policy ties service purchases to individual need, financial participation rules and other available funding. Do not promise universal free training or equipment. [Service funding policy](https://sites.google.com/state.co.us/dvr-policy-manual-v-102023/chapter-12-vocational-rehabilitation-services/12-1-scope-of-vr-services)

Detailed adult, contact and waitlist webpages were inaccessible during research. Exact Denver field-office arrangements and current individual cost rules remain unverified within the source-page ceiling.
openQuestions: What is the September 2026 waitlist status, and is the applicant's priority category being released?
Which Denver field office will handle intake, what documentation is needed, and when can assessment occur?
Which planned services require financial participation, and what employment assistance is available while waiting?
